riddle.question: What repeats your words without a mouth?
riddle.source: Fixed riddle of the supplied fake_llm_json (S2-03). The real game asks the LLM to invent its own riddle; this one makes the cases reproducible.

conventions.answer: Text typed by the player, sent as the answer field of POST /api/answer.
conventions.answer_recipe: Builds a long answer instead of writing it out: repeat the string count times.
conventions.expected: accepted or rejected: the verdict a correct judge must give (correct=true or correct=false).
conventions.ambiguous: true when the group has not agreed on the expected verdict; the case stays out of the binary score.
conventions.service_failure: Simulated incident raised by the evaluator: timeout or unavailable.
conventions.service_reply: Raw reply of the evaluator to simulate; anything other than exactly {correct: boolean, message: string} is a technical failure.
conventions.cancel_before_verdict: true when POST /api/cancel is sent while the dialogue is pending.
conventions.expected_http: Status and error code of the POST itself, when the request is refused.
conventions.expected_status: Dialogue status read with GET /api/state once the evaluation has finished (null = no dialogue).
conventions.note: These keys describe corpus cases. None of them is a field of an HTTP request.

scores.judgement: accepted/rejected cases only: number of verdicts equal to expected. Used by S2-03 with the real model.
scores.input: Refused requests: checked by S2-04 against the API; they never reach the evaluator.
scores.technical: Failures and cancellation: checked by S2-04 with a fake sphinx. A simulated failure is never counted as a wrong judgement.
